title: First Impressions
description: The introductory unit of the year, a toolbox rather than a lesson: choosing the right reference book (dictionary, dictionary of synonyms and antonyms, thesaurus, encyclopedia, pronunciation dictionary), naming what you are looking at (formal and colloquial English, synonym, antonym, collocation, phrasal verb, idiom, proofreading), building collocations with make, do, dark, light, new and first, reading phrasal verbs whose particle changes everything (put off, put aside, put away, put forward, give up, call off, come about, make up), understanding idiomatic expressions that no dictionary of single words can explain, telling British English from American English in accent, spelling and vocabulary, hearing the four sounds hidden behind the spelling ch and recognising homophones, homographs and homonyms, reading a text type from its signals (receipt, bibliography, advertisement, instructions for use, description of an item), reading large figures with a million, a billion and a trillion plus a plural noun, and naming cultures and languages with the prefixes mono-, bi- and multi-
